title: De Infantibus Baptizandis
author: Concilia Carthaginiensia

passages.original: ideoque pro defuncto sacrificium offerri, no- men apud altare nominari severe admodum interdicunt; ipsumque antecessorum suorum decretum hac synodali constitutione confirmant. Haec constant ex Cypriani epistola 66, qua sic ait : Graviter commoli sumus, ego et collegae mei, qui praesentes aderant, et compresbyteri nostri qui nobis assidebant, etc. Baron. anno 257, numero 13 et 14. Hoc eodem concilio Baptismum infantulorum in casu necessitatis ante octavum diem accelerandum esse, ad quorumdam dubitationem responsum esse videtur : maxime, quia concilium illud tempore Ecclesiae pacato celebratum, non sub Lucio, ut Veneta editio habet, seb potius circa initium Valeriani habitum fuisse, certo colligere liceat.
passages.english: and therefore they very strictly forbid that a sacrifice be offered for the deceased or that his name be named at the altar; and they confirm the decree of their predecessors itself by this synodal enactment. These things are established from Cyprian's Epistle 66, in which he speaks thus: "We were gravely disturbed, I and my colleagues who were present, and our fellow presbyters who sat with us," etc. Baronius, year 257, numbers 13 and 14. At this same council it appears that a reply was given to the doubt of certain persons, [namely] that the baptism of little infants, in case of necessity, ought to be hastened before the eighth day: especially since it may be gathered with certainty that that council was celebrated at a peaceful time for the Church, and was held not under Lucius, as the Venetian edition has it, but rather around the beginning of Valerian's [reign].
passages.notes: "commoli" read as "commoti" and "seb" as "sed" (scanning errors). "Lucius" is presumably Pope Lucius I; "Valerian" is the emperor.
